newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin turns tables on Clinton with get well note.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin turns tables on Clinton with get well note.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin sent a get well telegram to U.S. President Bill Clinton on Saturday, just weeks after receiving best wishes for his own health.
"I will be glad to see you as soon as your health permits," Yeltsin said, echoing the sentiments of world leaders during his struggle with heart problems over the past eight months.
Clinton, who had an operation for a knee injury on Friday, said afterwards it would not change his plans to meet Yeltsin in Helsinki next week.

The March 19-20 summit had been scheduled to take place in the United States but was moved to Finland to ease the strain on the recuperating Kremlin leader, who underwent heart bypass surgery in November and came down with pneumonia in January.
Yeltsin, 66, has got back some of his old spark in recent appearances and hopes the summit will quash any remaining doubts about his ability to rule Russia.
Clinton, who tore a tendon on his knee after falling early on Friday morning, said from hospital on Saturday that he was feeling "great".
